title: Resume after a mid-category interrupt skips the interrupted subcap and reports the state clean
observed: A subcap with evidence banked but no synthesis is classified `volleyed`. `kg_reader.py next` serves only `pending` subcaps, so on resume the interrupted subcap is not re-served; orient.py's next_card jumps past it. orient.py's `do_first` never names it. At end of category, when pending hits 0, orient prints next_card {} and do_first ['state clean - proceed to next_card'] while volleyed:1 remains open. kg_reader.py `next` does return {"done":false,"volleyed_open":[...]} at that point, but orient.py — the one command R32 makes every fresh or compacted agent run — never surfaces it.
measurement: Built /tmp/.../RUN_TEST with 686 selected subcaps (P1C1=47), appended evidence+synthesis for P1C1.1.1 and evidence-only for P1C1.1.2, then ran `orient.py --run $RUN --category P1C1`: state {closed:1, volleyed:1, pending:45}, next_card.id = 'P1C1.1.3' — not P1C1.1.2. Shrank the set to 3 subcaps and closed the third: orient printed do_first ['state clean - proceed to next_card'] and next_card {} with worklist {closed:2, volleyed:1}, while `kg_reader.py next` on the same state returned {"done":false,"volleyed_open":["P1C1.1.2"]}.
headless_consequence: An unattended agent obeying R32 ('run orient first; obey do_first') is told the state is clean and there is no next card, and closes the category with an unsynthesised subcap. The subcap is not pending, so it is never re-served; it is not closed, so it never reaches a synthesis gate; and floors_gate's --require-synthesis check only applies to floor-PASS subcaps, so a below-floor interrupted subcap escapes that too (synthesis_missing was [] in my run).

title: An omitted readiness reads GREEN, defeating the engine's own stated amber default and the multiplicative safety property
observed: platform_fit.py declares READINESS_DEFAULT = 'amber' with the comment 'Unknown readiness is AMBER, the honest middle. Green would reward a card that established nothing; red would punish silence into a lie.' Its only production caller defeats this twice: _readiness_token returns 'green' for an empty/None value, and CG-30's recompute independently does `r.get('readiness') or 'green'`. Because _readiness_token only ever emits green|amber|red — all three mapped in READINESS_MULTIPLIER — the amber fallback is unreachable dead code on the MCP path. Candidate.readiness also defaults to 'green' at the dataclass level. An unmapped phrase correctly reads red (that half of the prompt's prediction holds), but silence reads 1.00.
measurement: Ran readiness_multiplier over the vocabulary: green 1.00 / amber 0.85 / red 0.62, fits 56.80 / 48.30 / 35.20 on a fixed subtotal 0.5683 — multiplication confirmed. `_readiness_token(None)` -> 'green'; `_readiness_token('mostly fine probably')` -> 'red'. Mutating fit.py:83 'green'->'amber' turns test_an_absent_readiness_is_green_because_nothing_was_claimed red (1 failed, 36 passed of 37), so the behaviour is deliberate and pinned against the engine's written policy.
headless_consequence: The multiplicative shape was chosen to make the measured '95 of 470 cards scored hot with every prerequisite failing' defect impossible. Omitting the readiness field restores exactly that path: a card that establishes nothing about its prerequisites keeps the full 1.00 multiplier and can cross the 80 hot band. Under automation, omission is the default failure mode of an incomplete producer run, so the cheapest thing to write is the one that scores highest.

title: alignment_quote is worth 0.20 of the composite and is documented as 'never gated'

NEVER rewritten, and never gated.' There is no e_id beside it, no register_evidence lookup, and no gate ties it to a source. SG-V4 (prose grounding) is severity 'disclose', not 'block', and abstains to a recorded NOT_RUN below 5 centroid members.

headless_consequence: A producer that cannot find a stated objective has two options — omit alignment and lose up to 20 points to impact_fallback, or invent a quote and keep them. Nothing distinguishes the two outcomes downstream, so the unattended path rewards fabrication with the largest single score movement available on the page, and the fabricated sentence is then rendered to the client as the client's own words.

title: Peer medians are stored producer assertions on the serving tier, never reconciled with peer_scores; at subcap grain the column has no writer at all
observed: Ingestion honours invariant 8 exactly: persist.py recomputes the category-grain median from the named-peer scores beside it, records an artefact_disagreement observation when the workbook's stated median differs, and stores nothing derivable ('recomputed from named-peer scores; stated value not stored'). That discipline stops at the connector. heatmap_workbook_scores.peer_median is written straight from the producer's payload; CG-44 checks only that delta equals score minus peer_median; nothing recomputes peer_median from the peer_scores rows the same run holds. And subcap_scores.peer_median has no writer anywhere in the repo — the single INSERT lists 8 columns and peer_median is not one of them — so the view serving_subcaps exposes a peer_median column that is structurally always NULL.
measurement: `select table_name||'.'||column_name from information_schema.columns where column_name ~ 'peer'` -> 4 stored peer_median columns. writer_spec.json:61-62 `"column": "peer_median", "source": "item:peer_median"`. `grep -rn 'percentile_cont|median(' apps/api apps/mcp apps/worker packages migrations --include=*.py --include=*.sql` -> 1 hit, a worker test name. apps/worker/dma_worker/persist.py:653 INSERT INTO subcap_scores lists (run_id, subcap_id, capability_id, category_id, pillar_id, score, confidence, source_cell) — 8 columns, no peer_median; the only other writers are counts.py and migrations touching linked_evidence_count/thin flags. Ingestion discipline mutation-proven: replacing `if abs(mid - p["stated_median"]) > Decimal("0.005"):` with `if False:` turns test_persist_dedup.py::test_peer_scores_store_only_named_scores_and_verify_the_median red; restored, green.

The peer comparison a client forms on the overview strip is whatever the producing agent typed, and nothing can check it against the peer scores the run actually ingested even though get_report_bundle hands the agent that table. title: verify_deployed.py --quick reports a pass when it could read nothing, and deploy.sh cannot fail on the verdict
observed: The script's own docstring promises 'Exit 0 when the deployed bundle matches HEAD, 1 when it does not, 2 when the comparison could not be made — which is NOT a pass, and says so.' Full mode honours that: with no gcloud it prints three COULD NOT READ lines and exits 2. --quick mode prints the identical three COULD NOT READ lines and then 'No service has unshipped commits touching its source.' and exits 0. Separately, deploy.sh invokes it with `|| { echo ... >&2; }`, deliberately non-fatal, so even the correct exit 2 does not stop a release from reporting success.
measurement: `which gcloud` -> not found; the script resolves /root/google-cloud-sdk/bin/gcloud and gets ENOENT for all three services. `python3 scripts/verify_deployed.py --quick` -> 'dmai-web/api/mcp COULD NOT READ ...' then 'No service has unshipped commits touching its source.', exit 0. `python3 scripts/verify_deployed.py` -> same three lines then 'Could not read the web image digest — comparison NOT made. That is not a pass.', exit 2. `grep -n verify_deployed infra/deploy.sh` -> 480, 489, 491; call site is deploy.sh:489-495. HEAD f18cbd0 committed 2026-08-28T13:50:07+00:00.
headless_consequence: The charter's 'not done until live in prod' rests on this comparison. In an unattended deploy where the credential has expired, the SDK is missing, or Artifact Registry is unreachable, --quick returns green and the full mode's red is swallowed by the non-fatal call, so the release reports success with the bytes unverified — which is exactly the class of failure (shipped defect 13, four render fixes reported live against an older revision) the script was written to end. The production comparison itself is BLOCKED here: unblocking needs the gcloud SDK plus a service account with roles/run.viewer and roles/artifactregistry.reader on digital-maturity-assessor, then the full mode.

title: Nothing marks a DMA finished, and no line in the repo notices
observed: run_status_t has seven values and none of them means 'this assessment is complete and correct'. PROMOTED is the end of the road and is explicitly revisable — retention exists so a single page can be re-promoted at any time, and promote is documented as 'the ONLY way back from withdrawal'. SUPERSEDED and WITHDRAWN both mean 'no longer serving', not 'done'. runs.completed_at is not a lifecycle marker either: it is the assessment's stated completion date parsed out of the manifest at ingest, falling back to the date token inside the request id. The nearest thing to a lifecycle answer is the six-month refresh_due_date on serving_directory, and cadence.py never frames it as finality.
measurement: `select unnest(enum_range(null::run_status_t))` -> INGESTED, CLAIMED, SYNTHESISING, STAGED, PROMOTED, SUPERSEDED, WITHDRAWN (7 values). Status writers across the whole live tree: 3 — promote.py:370 (SUPERSEDED), promote.py:378 (PROMOTED), withdraw.py:89 (WITHDRAWN). `grep -rniE 'terminal state|final state|run is final|marks .* final' apps/api apps/mcp apps/worker packages migrations docs/text scripts` = 0 hits. apps/worker/dma_worker/persist.py:92 `_stated_completed_at` docstring confirms completed_at's ingest-time provenance.
headless_consequence: With no human deciding 'we are done with this client', finality is whatever the last unattended session happened to leave behind. A run that promoted with a disclosed SG failure, a thin page, or an open rejection sits in exactly the same state as one that is genuinely finished, and no query can separate them. Combined with the retention design there is no point at which an autonomous loop should stop working a run — so either it stops arbitrarily, or it never stops.

title: The rejection ledger is wired but has no unattended consumer
observed: The write path is proven end to end and the corpus-wide read exists as an MCP tool. What is missing is anything that drains the queue without a person or an agent choosing to look: the only non-agent caller in the repo is scripts/goal_status.py, an on-demand reporting script. The three Scheduler triggers (package scan, corpus-gate-scanner, pack-exporter) do not read it, and no alert, watchdog or Routine acts on a non-empty queue. Gate K, which guards the wiring, is a source-text gate by design ('Four claims, all read from source, no database'), so its pass proves the strings are present rather than that a row lands — which is why the end-to-end probe was necessary.
measurement: `grep -rn 'open_corpus_wide|list_open_rejections|rejection_ledger|open_rejections' scripts/ infra/ apps/worker plugins/dma-insights/{agents,hooks}` -> outside gate_k and its tests, the only executable caller is scripts/goal_status.py:87 `rej = call("list_open_rejections")`; every other hit is an agent frontmatter tools: list. The probe itself: a real failing submit produced 12 rejection_ledger rows and open_corpus_wide returned all 12 with summary {'open': 12, 'looping': 0, 'pages': ['overview']}.
headless_consequence: The queue is the only durable trace a refusal leaves once a session ends, and it is pull-only. Unattended, twelve open rejections on a client look exactly like zero until something calls the tool; the `looping` counter that would show 'this is the fourth attempt at the same reason' is computed and never read on a schedule. The mechanism is sound — what is absent is the reader.

title: Grain reconciles payload-against-served at 0.05, but never grain-against-grain
observed: CG-07 is a real, DB-backed, mutation-proven check: any object carrying a grain id and a numeric score is compared to that grain's served figure at 0.05, and a figure naming a grain the run serves nothing for is rejected outright. But _served_figures builds pillar and category figures as unweighted means of the run's own cells and then OVERWRITES them with the workbook's STATED grains ('A STATED grain always wins'). When the workbook states both a pillar figure and its category figures, both win and nothing compares them, so a pillar rollup that disagrees with the categories beneath it passes. The audit's own ledger line attributes grain reconciliation to scripts/gate_j_surface_parity.py, which does no such thing — its docstring says 'It never compares VALUES.'

title: Invariant 1's gate is a literal-import regex; three evasions to a live inference endpoint pass it
_section: §5.2 — the twelve invariants
observed: Invariant 1 ('no model calls at request time') is the most fundamental in the charter, and its guard is a literal-statement regex over a 13-entry blocklist: PY_IMPORT = ^\s*(?:import|from)\s+(anthropic|openai|cohere|...)\b. measurement: MUTATION RUN. title: The production colour resolver paints a grey swatch for a null score, violating invariants 6 and 9
